sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗马·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Back in 1989, the engineers of Japan's famous Shinkansen bullet train realized they had a problem.
sentences.zh: 早在1989年，日本著名的“新干线”子弹头列车的工程师们发现他们遇到了一个问题。

sentences.en: The train was moving so fast that when it went into a tunnel,
sentences.zh: 列车行驶速度极快，以至于当它驶入隧道时，

sentences.en: it basically punched the air out the far end, creating little sonic booMs.
sentences.zh: 它基本上把隧道另一端的空气猛烈挤压出去，产生了微型的声爆。

sentences.en: All across Japan, the Shinkansen was rattling buildings and disturbing residents in the neighborhoods it passed through.
sentences.zh: 在日本各地，新干线列车剧烈震动着建筑物，并打扰了它所穿过社区的居民。

sentences.en: An engineering team was brought in to design a quieter and more efficient train, and they had a secret weapon.
sentences.zh: 工程团队被请来设计一种更安静、更高效的列车，他们拥有一个秘密武器。

sentences.en: A.G.
sentences.zh: 还有

sentences.en: Nakatsu, the general manager of the technical development department, was a birdwatcher.
sentences.zh: 中津，技术开发部门的总经理，是一位观鸟爱好者。

sentences.en: As he thought about the redesign, Nakatsu took inspiration from elements of his favorite birds, including owl feathers and penguin bellies.
sentences.zh: 在思考重新设计时，中津从他最喜欢的鸟类的特征中汲取了灵感，包括猫头鹰的羽毛和企鹅的腹部。

sentences.en: But the bird that inspired the most important element of the redesign was the kingfisher.
sentences.zh: 但启发了这次重新设计中最重要部分的鸟类是翠鸟。

sentences.en: Kingfishers are famous for the elegant way they dive into the water to catch fish.
sentences.zh: 翠鸟因其优雅地潜入水中捕鱼的方式而闻名。

sentences.en: Their uniquely shaped beaks allow them to break the surface of the water with barely a splash.
sentences.zh: 它们形状独特的喙使它们能够破开水面，几乎不溅起水花。

sentences.en: And so Nakatsu and the Shinkansen design team decided to model the nose of their bullet trains off the kingfisher's beak.
sentences.zh: 因此，中津和新干线设计团队决定以翠鸟的喙为原型来设计子弹头列车的车鼻。

sentences.en: And it worked.
sentences.zh: 而且它成功了。

sentences.en: The new Shinkansen trains were quieter and more efficient.
sentences.zh: 新的新干线列车更加安静且高效。

sentences.en: That kingfisher redesign is now seen as a classic example of what's known as biomimicry.
sentences.zh: 翠鸟的这次重新设计现在被视为被称为“仿生学”的经典范例。

sentences.en: The act of looking to the non-human world for solutions to human design challenges.
sentences.zh: 从非人类世界中寻找人类设计挑战解决方案的行为。

sentences.en: Biomimicry is simply design that is inspired by nature.
sentences.zh: 仿生学就是受大自然启发的设计。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I have to say that stories about biomimicry are catnip to design journalists like me.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，关于仿生学的故事对像我这样的设计记者来说有着极大的吸引力。

sentences.en: That is Kurt Kolstad, our resident design guy.
sentences.zh: 那是柯特·科尔斯塔德，我们常驻的设计专家。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And biomimicry, it's just this really inspiring concept, right?
sentences.zh: 仿生学，这真是一个非常具有启发性的概念，对吧？

sentences.en: With all these fascinating examples, like the invention of Velcro being inspired by someone noticing how burrs stuck to his dog's fur and to his jacket while he was out on a walk.
sentences.zh: 有所有这些迷人的例子，比如尼龙搭扣的发明，灵感来自于某人在散步时注意到芒刺是如何粘在他的狗的毛和他的夹克上的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, I love these stories.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我喜欢这些故事。

sentences.en: We love these stories on the show.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中也喜欢这些故事。

sentences.en: We've covered biomimicry a lot over the years because the stories are just very catchy.
sentences.zh: 这些年来我们报道过很多次仿生学，因为这些故事非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: Like there is something so seductive about the idea of designers borrowing from nature to solve a human problem.
sentences.zh: 就像设计师从自然界借鉴灵感来解决人类问题这个想法，有一种非常诱人的魔力。

sentences.en: It's just a very neat, simple and just compelling narrative.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种非常干练、简单且引人入胜的叙事。

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: But recently, I've been digging into a bunch of biomimicry stories, and they are not always quite as neat and simple as that bullet train story.
sentences.zh: 但最近，我一直在深入研究一堆仿生学故事，它们并不总是像那个子弹头列车的故事那样干练和简单。

sentences.en: The causality is often quite a bit murkier than the headlines would have you believe.
sentences.zh: 因果关系往往比头条新闻让你相信的要模糊得多。

sentences.en: And the relationship between nature and human inspiration is often a lot more complicated.
sentences.zh: 自然与人类灵感之间的关系往往要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that actually makes biomimicry sound more interesting to me, not less.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上让仿生学听起来对我更有趣，而不是更少。

sentences.en: Like I like that idea of a complex story way better.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得那种复杂的故事构思好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree.
sentences.zh: 对，我同意。

sentences.en: Same here.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: So today we're going to dive deeper, go beyond some simple headlines, separate some fact from fiction, and yeah, go into some more nuanced cases.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我们要深入探讨，超越一些简单的头条新闻，去伪存真，并且探讨一些更微妙的案例。

sentences.en: To kick things off and ground us in the concept, I want to start with a relatively straightforward, yet lesser known example of biomimetic design.
sentences.zh: 为了开个好头并让我们对这个概念有切实的体会，我想从一个相对直接但鲜为人知的仿生设计例子开始。

sentences.en: So this story takes place in the early 1800s in London, England,
sentences.zh: 这个故事发生在19世纪初的英国伦敦，

sentences.en: which was not yet that modern city that we know with its sophisticated transit network or really even basic sanitation.
sentences.zh: 当时的伦敦还远不是我们今天所知道的那个拥有复杂交通网络、甚至连基本卫生设施都不完善的现代化城市。

sentences.en: But it was already the largest city that we know with us, but it was already the largest city in the world and the largest port in the world.
sentences.zh: 但它当时已经是我们所知的、也是世界上最大的人口城市和港口。

sentences.en: And when people needed to cross the city's famous Thames River near that port, they took the London Bridge.
sentences.zh: 当人们需要穿过该港口附近城市著名的泰晤士河时，他们会走伦敦桥。

sentences.en: But that bridge was notoriously crowded.
sentences.zh: 但那座桥出了名的拥挤。

sentences.en: It was like a choke point for everyday citizens and also commercial traffic, which really burdened people as well as, you know, the city's commerce.
sentences.zh: 它就像是普通市民和商业交通的瓶颈，这确实给人们以及城市的商业带来了沉重的负担。

sentences.en: And so over time, it became clear that another crossing downstream was desperately needed.
sentences.zh: 因此随着时间推移，人们越来越清楚地意识到，迫切需要在下游再建一个过河通道。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 对，这对我来说挺合理的。

sentences.en: They needed another bridge.
sentences.zh: 他们需要另一座桥。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: Except with the geography of the river and the port and the existing bridge, another bridge would have interfered severely with shipping access.
sentences.zh: 只是考虑到河流、港口和现有桥梁的地理情况，再建一座桥会严重干扰航运通行。

sentences.en: So that solution was a non-starter.
sentences.zh: 所以这个方案行不通。

sentences.en: And the only real alternative was to tunnel under the river.
sentences.zh: 唯一的现实替代方案是在河底下挖隧道。

sentences.en: But this is way before the tunnel to France or even the London Underground.
sentences.zh: 但这远在通往法国的隧道甚至伦敦地铁出现之前。

sentences.en: So there was no precedent for tunnels going under active waterways.
sentences.zh: 因此，先前没有任何在通航水道下方修建隧道的先例。

sentences.en: Tunneling technology at this point was essentially an extension of mining technology, right?
sentences.zh: 当时的掘进技术本质上只是采矿技术的延伸，对吧？

sentences.en: Dealing with solid rock and soil, but not the undersides of rivers.
sentences.zh: 主要用于处理坚硬的岩石和土壤，而不是河流的底部。

sentences.en: And so they tried to use those surface traditional mining techniques to tunnel under the Thames, but it ended in disaster and in some cases the deaths of workers.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们试图利用这些传统的地面采矿技术在泰晤士河下方掘进，但结果却是一场灾难，在某些情况下甚至导致了工人的死亡。

sentences.en: And experts eventually came to conclude that this type of tunnel represented an impossible challenge.
sentences.zh: 专家们最终得出结论，这种类型的隧道代表了一项不可能完成的挑战。

sentences.en: An engineer named Mark Brunel even wrote that prior attempts, quote, had so completely failed that he conceived all further exertions on the subject quite fruitless,
sentences.zh: 一位名叫马克·布鲁内尔的工程师甚至写道，先前的尝试“彻底失败了，以至于他认为所有进一步的努力都是徒劳的”，

sentences.en: as in it would be pointless to even try.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，甚至连尝试都毫无意义。

sentences.en: But Brunel was about to have an experience that would completely change his mind.
sentences.zh: 但布鲁内尔即将经历一件彻底改变他想法的事。

sentences.en: Okay, so what happened?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's best if I let him explain it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得最好还是让他自己来解释。

sentences.en: So here's an excerpt from a letter that he wrote to his granddaughter later on, recalling his time working for the British Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 这是他后来写给孙女的一封信的摘录，回忆了他当时在英国皇家海军工作的经历。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to have you read it.
sentences.zh: 我这就让你来读一下。

sentences.en: About the year 1812, being then employed in the dockyard at Chatham, I happened to see before me a piece of condemned timber, a portion of the keel of a ship, wherein the worm,
sentences.zh: 大约在1812年，当时我在查塔姆船厂工作，我碰巧看到眼前有一块被判废弃的木料，是一艘船的龙骨的一部分，里面有虫子，

sentences.en: the Teredo Novalis, had made many erosions.
sentences.zh: 也就是船蛆，蛀出了许多孔洞。

sentences.en: And by erosions, he means tunnels, like tunnels through the wood.
sentences.zh: 他说的“孔洞”其实就是隧道，就像在木头里打洞一样。

sentences.en: Okay, so in modern English, like he saw a piece of timber that had been worm-eaten along the docks.
sentences.zh: 好吧，用现代英语来说，就像他在码头上看到了一块被虫蛀过的木头。

sentences.en: Yeah, pretty much, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 对，差不多，基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: Except that the so-called naval shipworm is not actually a worm.
sentences.zh: 只不过这种所谓的船蛆实际上并不是真正的虫子。

sentences.en: In reality, it's a strangely adapted bivalve mollusk.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它是一种经过奇特演化的双壳软体动物。

sentences.en: Oh, like a clam.
sentences.zh: 哦，就像一只蛤蜊。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, except specialized for boring holes.
sentences.zh: 对，对，只不过是专门用来钻孔的。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And it works like this.
sentences.zh: 而且它是这样运作的。

sentences.en: Like its shell has evolved into a pair of grinding plates.
sentences.zh: 就像它的外壳进化成了一对研磨板。

sentences.en: And behind those plates trails this long, soft, elongated body that can reach a couple of feet in length.
sentences.zh: 在这两块板的后面，拖着这个长而柔软、细长的身体，长度可以达到好几英尺。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds terrifying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来挺吓人的。

sentences.en: It sounds something that I would eat eventually as an appetizer.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是我最后会当成开胃菜吃掉的东西。

sentences.en: Hopefully, right?
sentences.zh: 希望如此吧？

sentences.en: Hopefully it wouldn't eat you, right?
sentences.zh: 希望它不会把你吃掉，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you put some mignonette on it, you know, like you scrape it out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你往上面加点红葱头醋汁，你知道的，就像把它刮出来一样。

sentences.en: It's going to be tasty.
sentences.zh: 这会很好吃的。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: He didn't go quite that far, but he did pull out a magnifying glass, which is a thing that he was known to carry around, and went in for a closer look.
sentences.zh: 他没有走得那么远，但他确实掏出一个放大镜——这是他随身携带的标志性物品——然后凑近仔细观察。

sentences.en: And as he looked, he noticed that the walls of these boreholes that were carved by these worms seemed remarkably stable.
sentences.zh: 当他仔细观察时，他注意到这些由虫子钻出来的钻孔内壁显得异常稳固。

sentences.en: Even when they were in waterlogged and, like, rotting chunks of wood from old ships, they were protected.
sentences.zh: 即使它们身处浸水且像是在旧船上腐烂的木头块中，它们也受到了保护。

sentences.en: So here's Brunel again from that same letter.
sentences.zh: 所以布鲁内尔在同一封信中又写道。

sentences.en: I then said to myself that these little things have made little tunnels.
sentences.zh: 我当时对自己说，这些小东西开凿出了小小的隧道。

sentences.en: So might we by adopting some corresponding means of protection.
sentences.zh: 那么我们是否也可以通过采用某种相应的保护手段来实现呢？

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically, like, the textbook definition of biomimicry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上就是仿生学的教科书式定义。

sentences.en: So what did Brunel notice about how the shipworms made their tunnels?
sentences.zh: 那么，关于船蛆是如何建造它们的隧道的，布鲁内尔注意到了什么？

sentences.en: So the trick that he recognized and then set out to copy was that shipworms do two things at the same time.
sentences.zh: 他认识到并随后着手模仿的诀窍在于，船蛆同时做两件事。

sentences.en: Even as they scrape out the wood in front of them and move forward into that hole, they extrude a lining that coats and reinforces the tunnel around and behind them.
sentences.zh: 就在它们刮掉前方木头并向前钻入那个洞的同时，它们分泌出一层内衬，用来涂抹并加固它们周围及身后的隧道。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So while they dig, they also immediately shore up the tunnel around them, which describes basically all excavation.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们在挖掘的同时，也立即加固了周围的隧道，这基本上描述了所有的挖掘工作。

sentences.en: So how is this different from other attempts?
sentences.zh: 那么，这与其他尝试有何不同？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so think of it this way, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这么想吧，对吧？

sentences.en: Miners used to working in hard soil could get away with digging for a stretch and then stopping for a bit and then going back and putting up supports behind them.
sentences.zh: 过去在坚硬土壤中工作的矿工可以先挖上一段，然后停一会儿，再回去在身后架设支撑物。

sentences.en: And Brunel recognized that that kind of iterative system just was not going to cut it under the Thames because any gap in space or time between digging and shoring up invited disaster.
sentences.zh: 而布鲁内尔认识到，这种迭代系统在泰晤士河底根本行不通，因为挖掘和加固之间任何空间或时间的间隙都会招致灾难。

sentences.en: And so with that in mind, in 1818, he went and patented a machine that would work more like a shipworm, digging and then reinforcing simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 因此，带着这个想法，在1818年，他去申请了一台机器的专利，这台机器的工作原理更像船蛆，即同时进行挖掘和加固。

sentences.en: So how did Brunel's machine do that?
sentences.zh: 那么布鲁内尔的机器是如何做到这一点的呢？

sentences.en: Well, the crucial piece was what he called a tunneling shield.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最关键的部分是他所称的盾构机（隧道盾构）。

sentences.en: Basically, it was this massive cast iron frame that was pressed flush against the face of the excavation.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这是一个巨大的铸铁框架，紧紧贴着挖掘面压紧。

sentences.en: And under that shield, you would have dozens of miners chipping away at the front of the tunnel while bricklayers shored up the tunnel behind them.
sentences.zh: 在这个盾构下方，会有数十名矿工在隧道前方凿岩，而泥水匠则在他们身后的隧道进行加固。

sentences.en: So as the excavation progressed, the shield would be pushed forward and the newly exposed sections were immediately lined with cemented bricks.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着挖掘的推进，盾构会被向前推，新露出的部分会立即用粘合的砖块进行衬砌。

sentences.en: And so it was all part of this smooth and continuous effort like the shipworm tunneling and shoring up behind itself simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一切都是这种顺利且持续努力的一部分，就像船蛆一边打洞，一边在身后同时进行加固一样。

sentences.en: That's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and really challenging because, you know,
sentences.zh: 对啊，而且真的很有挑战性，因为你知道，

sentences.en: Brunel had to piece together this system from all these moving parts and people because the technology at the time was not up to making like a machine that could automate all of this,
sentences.zh: 布鲁内尔必须把这个由各种活动部件和人员组成的系统拼凑起来，因为当时的科技还不足以制造出能实现这一切自动化的机器，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: It had to be people doing manual labor.
sentences.zh: 只能靠人工来完成。

sentences.en: And ultimately, it worked.
sentences.zh: 最终，它成功了。

sentences.en: It took a really long time and it did not always go smoothly.
sentences.zh: 这花了很长时间，而且并非总是一帆风顺。

sentences.en: But eventually, Brunel completed the tunnel spanning over a thousand feet under the Thames in 1843.
sentences.zh: 但最终，布鲁内尔在1843年完成了这条横跨泰晤士河底、长达一千多英尺的隧道。

sentences.en: And that was the first tunnel built underneath a river anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 那是世界上第一条在河流底下建造的隧道。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, no, like it was literally, pardon the pun, groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，不，就像它真的是——请原谅这个双关语——开创性的。

sentences.en: Nobody on Earth had ever made and walked through a tunnel like this before.
sentences.zh: 地球上从来没有人建造并穿过这样一条隧道。

sentences.en: And it didn't stop there because Brunel's design, that tunnel shield, shaped subsequent tunneling technology.
sentences.zh: 而且还不止于此，因为布鲁内尔的设计，那个盾构机，塑造了后来的隧道掘进技术。

sentences.en: Years later, when they built out subway systems in London and across the pond in New York, they used that same basic tunnel shield.
sentences.zh: 多年后，当他们在伦敦和大洋彼岸的纽约建造地铁系统时，他们使用的就是那个基本的盾构机。

sentences.en: That's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: And the funny thing is, modern machines have, if anything, converged even more on those mollusks that originally inspired Brunel.
sentences.zh: 更有趣的是，现代机器甚至在更大程度上向当初启发了布鲁内尔的那些软体动物靠拢了。

sentences.en: Because now we have machines with attachments that place precast concrete panels as the borer tunnels onward.
sentences.zh: 因为现在我们的机器带有能在掘进机向前推进时安装预制混凝土面板的附件。

sentences.en: So it is like that all in one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像那种集多种功能于一体的东西。

sentences.en: Okay, so despite all the setbacks, we are really talking about a very straightforward case of biomimicry, like nature inspiring a human design.
sentences.zh: 好的，尽管有种种挫折，我们实际上谈论的是一个非常直接的仿生学案例，就像大自然启发了人类设计一样。

sentences.en: A guy sees something in nature, copies it, perfects it, boom, success.
sentences.zh: 一个人在大自然中发现了某个东西，模仿它，完善它，轰，成功。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's why I wanted to start here, honestly, because I wanted to ground us in a success story where nature really was this direct inspiration for a human design.
sentences.zh: 是的，老实说，这就是我想从这里开始的原因，因为我想让我们扎根于一个成功的案例，在这个案例中，大自然真正成为了人类设计的直接灵感来源。

sentences.en: But there are a lot of other stories that don't perfectly follow that neat, direct trajectory.
sentences.zh: 但还有很多其他的故事并没有完全遵循这种整洁、直接的发展轨迹。

sentences.en: Stories where the relationship between nature and human design inspiration is not quite so clear cut.
sentences.zh: 在这些故事中，自然与人类设计灵感之间的关系并没有那么清晰明了。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'm very excited to muddy the waters a little bit.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我非常高兴能把水搅浑一点。

sentences.en: So what is next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来是什么？

sentences.en: Well, a different sort of fishy biomimicry with some real twists and strange turns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一种不同类型的鱼类仿生学，其中包含一些真正的转折和奇妙的曲折。

sentences.en: Starting back in 2005, when Mercedes-Benz made a big splash with their Bionic, which was this new concept car that boasted a biomimetic origin story.
sentences.zh: 时间回到2005年，当时梅赛德斯-奔驰凭借其“仿生”概念车（Bionic）引起了巨大轰动，这是一款拥有仿生学起源故事的全新概念车。

sentences.en: They claimed their design was the first of its kind to attempt a, quote, complete transfer from nature to technology, end quote.
sentences.zh: 他们声称自己的设计是同类设计中的首创，试图实现所谓的“从自然到技术的完全转化”。

sentences.en: Well, that sounds like vague nonsense.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是一堆含糊不清的废话。

sentences.en: Yeah, a little bit.
sentences.zh: 是的，有点像。

sentences.en: I don't even know what that means.
sentences.zh: 我都不知道那是什么意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, the argument was essentially that biomimicry usually involves borrowing like a single feature or behavior from an animal, like a bird's feather or a whale's fin.
sentences.zh: 对的，嗯，他们的论点基本上是，仿生学通常涉及从动物身上借用单一的特征或行为，比如鸟类的羽毛或鲸鱼的鳍。

sentences.en: But that their new car was modeled on an entire organism, the boxfish.
sentences.zh: 但他们的新车是以整个生物体——箱鲀为蓝本设计的。

sentences.en: Here's a picture of it.
sentences.zh: 这是它的照片。

sentences.en: If you're picturing a boxy fish because it's called a boxfish, you're right on the money.
sentences.zh: 如果你脑海中浮现出一条方头方脑的鱼，因为它的名字叫箱鲀，那你可真是猜对了。

sentences.en: I mean, like it is a floating cube with fins.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就像是一个长着鳍的漂浮立方体。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's part of this family of really awkwardly angular fish, including the cowfish and the trunkfish.
sentences.zh: 它是这种非常笨拙且有棱角的鱼类家族的一部分，其中包括牛鲀和角箱鲀。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, compared to the naval shipworm, this thing is adorable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，跟海军船蛆比起来，这东西简直太可爱了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like bright yellow with spots on it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它通体亮黄，上面还有斑点。

sentences.en: But I have to admit, this thing doesn't look aerodynamic at all.
sentences.zh: 但我得承认，这东西看起来一点也不符合空气动力学。

sentences.en: Like, this seems like the opposite of an animal that you'd model a car on.
sentences.zh: 就好像，这简直是那种你绝不会用来作为汽车设计模特的动物的反面。

sentences.en: So what was the logic behind modeling a vehicle on this boxy shape?
sentences.zh: 那么，把车辆设计成这种方盒子形状背后的逻辑是什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, big picture, you know, the engineers at Mercedes were into this idea of biomimicry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从宏观来看，你知道的，梅赛德斯的工程师们当时对这种仿生学理念很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so they started scouring the animal kingdom for inspiration.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始在动物王国里搜寻灵感。

sentences.en: And they wondered if a fish, for example, could provide that inspiration for a car design.
sentences.zh: 他们纳闷，比如鱼类是否能为汽车设计提供这种灵感。

sentences.en: But cars have to be boxy.
sentences.zh: 但汽车必须得是方方正正的。

sentences.en: They're spaces that house humans.
sentences.zh: 它们是容纳人类的空间。

sentences.en: And a long, sleek fish is just never going to translate into a functional car.
sentences.zh: 而一条修长流线型的鱼是绝对无法转化成一辆实用汽车的。

sentences.en: And so if there is a boxy fish that has evolved to be aerodynamic and boxy, that really could be a breakthrough that works all around.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有一种方头方脑的鱼，在进化中兼顾了空气动力学和方形体态，那这绝对可能是一个各方面都行得通的突破。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But what made them think that the boxfish was aerodynamic?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么让他们觉得箱鲀符合空气动力学呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it started with some real serious scientific research that they came across that was being done into the boxfish.
sentences.zh: 对，嗯，这始于他们偶然发现的一些关于箱鲀的非常严肃的科学研究。

sentences.en: In particular, a study being run by a team spanning UCLA, Caltech, and Woods Hole.
sentences.zh: 特别是加州大学洛杉矶分校、加州理工学院和伍兹霍尔研究所的跨学科团队正在进行的一项研究。

sentences.en: And so they discovered that there are nuances to the shape of the boxfish that help stabilize it.
sentences.zh: 于是他们发现，箱鲀的体形有许多能帮助其保持稳定的微妙细节。

sentences.en: But basically, boxfish have these ridges that are called keels that run along their sides.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，箱鲀身体两侧有被称为龙骨的脊突。

sentences.en: And these help create little eddies, which help them course correct as they swim through the water.
sentences.zh: 这些结构有助于产生微小的漩涡，帮助它们在水中游动时修正方向。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Which I suppose is what you want to keep a car running smoothly, like on a highway.
sentences.zh: 我想这就好比你想让汽车平稳运行一样，比如在高速公路上。

sentences.en: It's like you want it to be stable.
sentences.zh: 就像你希望它保持稳定一样。

sentences.en: So that makes some sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这倒也说得通。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And after reading the peer-reviewed research papers, Mercedes engineers even reached out and called up one of the researchers to learn more about their study.
sentences.zh: 在阅读了同行评审的研究论文后，梅赛德斯的工程师甚至主动联系并致电其中一位研究人员，以了解更多关于他们研究的信息。

sentences.en: And then they took it a step further and did research of their own.
sentences.zh: 然后他们更进一步，自己也做了研究。

sentences.en: They had drag tests around 3D models of these fish that suggested that despite their squarish face, they were surprisingly streamlined, at least in controlled conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些鱼的三维模型进行了风阻测试，结果表明，尽管它们长着方头方脑的脸，但出人意料地具有流线型，至少在受控条件下是这样。

sentences.en: And so, in the end, Mercedes designers concluded that the boxfish, for all of its boxiness, represented a, quote, aerodynamic ideal, end quote.
sentences.zh: 因此，最终梅赛德斯的设计师们得出结论，箱鲀尽管浑身是方块状，却代表了一种所谓“空气动力学理想状态”。

sentences.en: And the Bionic is the car that they built, the Mercedes.
sentences.zh: 而仿生概念车就是他们制造的那辆车，梅赛德斯的汽车。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: They didn't just design it.
sentences.zh: 他们不只是设计了它。

sentences.en: They actually built it.
sentences.zh: 他们真的把它造出来了。

sentences.en: And here's a picture of what it looks like, right?
sentences.zh: 这里有一张它长什么样子的图片，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a car which, true to its inspiration, is relatively boxy, as you can see.
sentences.zh: 正如你所看到的，正如它的灵感来源一样，这辆车相对比较方正。

sentences.en: And it also has these angled ridges along the side that came from the boxfish, more or less.
sentences.zh: 它车身侧面也有那些基本上源自箱鲀的倾斜棱脊。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I mean, so I'm looking at a picture now.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我现在正在看一张图片。

sentences.en: It is definitely boxy.
sentences.zh: 这车确实挺方正的。

sentences.en: It's pretty cute.
sentences.zh: 它挺可爱的。

sentences.en: I mean, it sort of looks like a lime green VW bug with, you know, some more squarish features, kind of like a van bug, you know, kind of.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它看起来有点像青柠绿的大众甲壳虫，你知道的，线条更方正一些，有点像厢式货车和甲壳虫的结合体，差不多是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great description.
sentences.zh: 对，这个形容太贴切了。

sentences.en: And honestly, I also think it's pretty cute.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我也觉得它挺可爱的。

sentences.en: And I'm not the only one.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是我这么觉得。

sentences.en: When Mercedes put this car out into the world in the spotlight at a big public event, it was a hit.
sentences.zh: 当梅赛德斯在一次大型公开活动中把这款车隆重推出时，它一炮而红。

sentences.en: The Bionic design got featured in Nat Geo.
sentences.zh: 仿生设计登上了《国家地理》杂志。

sentences.en: It was, like, installed in the MoMA.
sentences.zh: 它甚至被纳⼊了现代艺术博物馆（MoMA）展出。

sentences.en: And for a while, it was probably the most widely circulated example of automotive biomimicry in the world.
sentences.zh: 在一段时间里，它可能是世界上流传最广的汽车仿生学案例。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I haven't seen one of these, so I'm assuming it never got out of the concept car stage, right?
sentences.zh: 对，但我没见过这车，所以我猜它从来没走出概念车阶段吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: There is no commercial car that evolved out of this.
sentences.zh: 没有任何市售车是由此演变而来的。

sentences.en: The Bionic was really never truly made to go on the roads.
sentences.zh: “仿生”车实际上从未真正打算上路行驶。

sentences.en: It was just a concept car that got a bunch of attention and had a bunch of stories written about it.
sentences.zh: 它只是一款吸引了大量关注并引发无数报道的概念车。

sentences.en: But, you know, like, that, from their perspective, was kind of the whole idea in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，从他们的角度来看，这本来就是最初的整体构想。

sentences.en: Mercedes might not have gotten a commercial car to sell, but they did get this great story that helped associate their brand with being, like,
sentences.zh: 梅赛德斯可能没有造出一款可供销售的量产车，但他们确实收获了一个极佳的故事，有助于将他们的品牌形象塑造得像

sentences.en: eco-friendly and cutting-edge and tied into this legacy of natural design that had evolved in, like, the organic elements over the eons.
sentences.zh: 环保且前沿，并与历经数亿年漫长岁月在有机元素中演化而来的自然设计传统紧密相连。

sentences.en: Okay, but so far this seems like a pretty straightforward biomimicry story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但到目前为止，这似乎还是一个相当直观的仿生学故事。

sentences.en: Well, it would be if the story ended there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果故事到此为止的话确实如此。

sentences.en: And for Mercedes, it basically did.
sentences.zh: 对梅赛德斯来说，基本上也确实如此。

sentences.en: But the fish scientists, like scientists do, kept going.
sentences.zh: 但鱼类科学家们像往常一样，继续深入研究。

sentences.en: And 10 years after the Bionic's big reveal, researchers with new technologies published new findings that painted a very different picture.
sentences.zh: 在“仿生”车首次亮相10年后，拥有新技术的研宄人员发表了新的发现，描绘了一幅截然不同的画卷。

sentences.en: The old data wasn't wrong exactly.
sentences.zh: 旧数据倒也不是完全错误。

sentences.en: It was just woefully incomplete.
sentences.zh: 只是极其不完整。

sentences.en: And long story short, it turns out that the boxfish, in its totality, is definitely not a, quote, aerodynamic ideal.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，事实证明，箱鲀从整体来看，绝对不是什么所谓的“空气动力学理想模型”。

sentences.en: In fact, if anything, it's basically the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，硬要说的话，它基本上完全相反。

sentences.en: So what did they find out?
sentences.zh: 那么他们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the new team, led by a biomorphology researcher named Sam Van Wassenberg, modeled that blunt, boxy front, plowing head-on through the water.
sentences.zh: 嗯，由生物形态学研究员萨姆·范瓦森贝赫领导的新团队，对那张钝平、方正的前脸在水中迎头破浪的形态进行了建模。

sentences.en: And look, it does do okay aerodynamically.
sentences.zh: 你看，从空气动力学角度来看，它表现确实还行。

sentences.en: As Mercedes had concluded, if it's going straightforward.
sentences.zh: 正如梅赛德斯得出的结论那样，如果它是直线前进的话。

sentences.en: But as soon as the fish turns its head, its aerodynamics are totally destabilized.
sentences.zh: 但只要这条鱼一转头，它的空气动力学性能就会彻底失稳。

sentences.en: Which doesn't sound like a great model for a car.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可不是汽车的理想模仿对象。

sentences.en: Yeah, or definitely not the one they were envisioning.
sentences.zh: 对，或者说绝对不是他们设想的那种。

sentences.en: Because it turns out that the boxfish's superpower is maneuverability, not aerodynamics.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明，箱鲀的超级能力是机动性，而不是空气动力学。

sentences.en: And if you actually watch them, they're not straight-line swimmers or speed racers.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细观察它们，就会发现它们既不是直线游泳健将，也不是赛车手。

sentences.en: They are these reef fish.
sentences.zh: 它们是这种珊瑚礁鱼类。

sentences.en: And they spend their days threading their way through reefs and evading predators.
sentences.zh: 它们白天在珊瑚礁中穿梭，躲避掠食者。

sentences.en: These are animals that need to turn on a dime.
sentences.zh: 这些动物需要能够瞬间灵活转向。

sentences.en: So they're super agile, and they flick their fins and rotate themselves in three dimensions, which is very cool and totally useful to them.
sentences.zh: 所以它们超级敏捷，会摆动鱼鳍并在三维空间中旋转，这非常酷，对它们也完全有用。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it's not what you're looking for in a car.
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，这并不是你对一辆汽车的要求。

sentences.en: With a car, you want a shape that can travel fast and, you know, run smooth in one direction, even in high winds, just sort of stay on course.
sentences.zh: 对于汽车，你需要的是一种能够快速行驶的形状，而且你知道的，在单一方向上平稳运行，即使在大风中也能保持航向。

sentences.en: And the boxfish, for those purposes, was essentially the worst fish to choose.
sentences.zh: 而就这些用途而言，箱鲀可以说是最糟糕的选择。

sentences.en: So the Bionic, it came out.
sentences.zh: 所以，仿生车发布了。

sentences.en: It had a big splash.
sentences.zh: 它引起了很大的轰动。

sentences.en: It was, like, sent around, I'm sure, online a lot.
sentences.zh: 它就像是被四处转发，我确信在网上有很多。

sentences.en: When the new research came out, did Mercedes respond to it at all?
sentences.zh: 当新研究出来时，梅赛德斯对此有什么回应吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no, no, not at all.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，不，完全没有。

sentences.en: And, in fact, the Bionic's official web page still describes the boxfish as having a, quote, highly streamlined body shape.
sentences.zh: 事实上，仿生车的官方网页仍然将箱鲀描述为拥有“高度流线型的车身形状”。

sentences.en: Wait, so they still have a web page for this thing?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以他们还在为这东西保留网页？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's still up there.
sentences.zh: 对，它还在那里。

sentences.en: It's still, like, part of their marketing material.
sentences.zh: 它仍然像是他们营销材料的一部分。

sentences.en: It's, like, the story of this thing was always the point.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，这东西的故事本身才是重点。

sentences.en: It was never about whether the car actually worked.
sentences.zh: 这从来都不是关于这辆车是否真的能开。

sentences.en: So this kind of biomimicry story, would you classify it as more typical than, like, the TAM's tunnel success?
sentences.zh: 所以这类仿生学故事，你觉得它比像TAM隧道成功那样的案例更典型吗？

sentences.en: Like, is this the type of thing that is mostly what happens when we try to use biomimetic design?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这正是我们尝试运用仿生设计时通常会出现的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say that, you know, failures are definitely more common than successes.
sentences.zh: 对，我会说，你知道，失败绝对比成功更常见。

sentences.en: But there's also, like, other kinds of non-successes, like, basically sort of fake stories of having biomimetic inspiration.
sentences.zh: 但也有其他类型的“非成功”情况，比如，基本上就是那种假装拥有仿生灵感的虚构故事。

sentences.en: Or at least, like, vastly simplified ones, right?
sentences.zh: 或者至少可以说是被严重简化了的版本，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, just telling a biomimicry story about a product just so it sounds more interesting.
sentences.zh: 比如，仅仅为了让产品听起来更有趣，就硬编一个仿生学的故事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of those.
sentences.zh: 而且这种案例非常多。

sentences.en: And a classic example is this startup that claimed to have invented a water bottle based on the Namib Desert Beetle,
sentences.zh: 一个经典的例子是一家初创公司，声称自己发明了一款基于纳米布沙漠甲虫的水壶，

sentences.en: which is this insect that has actually evolved a way to capture water out of thin air.
sentences.zh: 这种昆虫确实进化出了一种从稀薄空气中捕获水分的方法。

sentences.en: It collects and combines droplets on its back, and then those trickle down to its mouth so it can drink them.
sentences.zh: 它在背上收集并汇聚水滴，然后这些水滴流到嘴里供它饮用。

sentences.en: And so these water bottles were, you know, going to do that same thing, essentially, and fill themselves up.
sentences.zh: 所以这些水壶，你知道的，基本上就是打算做到同样的事情，然后自己装满水。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But since I haven't heard of a self-filling water bottle, I assume that that just didn't work.
sentences.zh: 但既然我没听说过什么会自动装满水的水壶，我猜那根本没成功。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, no.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，没有。

sentences.en: It did not actually work.
sentences.zh: 它确实没成功。

sentences.en: But it did get so much coverage in Wired and NPR and BBC, and, like, the list goes on.
sentences.zh: 但它确实在《连线》杂志、NPR和BBC上获得了极高的报道度，而且名单还长得很。

sentences.en: They even raised millions of dollars on the backs of those beetles.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至靠这些甲虫赚了几百万美元。

sentences.en: So, yeah, the water bottle, like the bionic, it was really more about PR than real biomimicry.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那个水瓶，就像仿生汽车一样，与其说是真正的仿生学，不如说是为了公关。

sentences.en: And, honestly, it had less pretensions to even tie to science, I think, than the bionic did.
sentences.zh: 而且老实说，我觉得它比仿生汽车更少标榜自己与科学的联系。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Okay, so we have one example of successful biomimicry with the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们有一个关于隧道成功仿生学的例子。

sentences.en: We have the Mercedes example, which is really, you know, a success in marketing, but not really as successful as a product.
sentences.zh: 我们有梅赛德斯的例子，你知道，这在营销上确实是个成功，但作为产品却算不上真正成功。

sentences.en: So, what's next?
sentences.zh: 那么，接下来是什么？

sentences.en: Something that is, honestly, a little more complicated and less straightforward than either of those.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是一个比前面两个都要复杂一些、不那么直截了当的例子。

sentences.en: Okay, we'll get to that after the break.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们休息一下再继续。

sentences.en: So, we're back talking about biomimicry with Kurt Kolstad.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，我们继续和库尔特·科尔斯特德一起探讨仿生学。

sentences.en: So, our final story is about a structural design that you can find basically anywhere in the aerospace industry.
sentences.zh: 我们的最后一个故事讲的是一种结构设计，你基本上可以在航空航天业的任何地方找到它。

sentences.en: If you peel back a panel on a Boeing plane or a NASA shuttle, you'll see an array of hexagons.
sentences.zh: 如果你剥开波音飞机或美国宇航局航天飞机上的一块面板，你会看到排列整齐的六边形。

sentences.en: And these are called honeycomb sandwich panels.
sentences.zh: 这些被称为蜂窝夹层板。

sentences.en: They look like and will instantly remind you of beehives.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来就像蜂窝，会立刻让你联想到蜂巢。

sentences.en: Yeah, so honeycomb panels, I've definitely seen them before.
sentences.zh: 是的，蜂窝板，我以前绝对见过。

sentences.en: I think anyone who's paid attention to structures at all have seen them before.
sentences.zh: 我想任何稍微注意过结构的人以前都见过。

sentences.en: Were they inspired by bees?
sentences.zh: 它们的灵感来自蜜蜂吗？

sentences.en: Well, that seemingly simple question is actually surprisingly difficult to answer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个看似简单的问题其实出奇地难以回答。

sentences.en: Because if you think about it, like, people have been admiring and examining honeycombs since ancient times.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你仔细想想，人们自古以来就一直在赞赏和研究蜂窝。

sentences.en: Like, the earliest written account we have of why they might create hexagonal shapes dates back to 37 BC.
sentences.zh: 比如说，我们找到关于它们为什么会建造六边形的最早文字记载可以追溯到公元前37年。

sentences.en: And it was around this time that geometers had figured out that hexagons are one of only three shapes that you can tile continuously and without gaps.
sentences.zh: 大约也是在这个时候，几何学家们发现六边形是能够连续且无缝拼接的仅有的三种形状之一。

sentences.en: There are squares, which, of course, you can visualize in a grid.
sentences.zh: 还有正方形，当然，你可以在网格中想象出来。

sentences.en: Yeah, like our logo.
sentences.zh: 对，就像我们的标志那样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah, and triangles, which, like, if you, you know, can picture a truss or if you just kind of alternate up and down, you can see those tiling forever, right?
sentences.zh: 对，还有三角形，如果你，你知道的，能想象出一个桁架，或者只是上下交替，你就能看到它们可以无限延伸地拼接，对吧？

sentences.en: And then there are hexagons.
sentences.zh: 然后就是六边形。

sentences.en: And of all that set, hexagons are the ones that give you the most space, as in the most area per unit of edge.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些形状中，六边形能提供最多的空间，也就是单位边缘长度下拥有最大的面积。

sentences.en: Which means that if you're tiling an array of shapes, these are the ones that let you use the least material.
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你要拼接一组形状，这种形状能让你使用最少的材料。

sentences.en: So for bees, that's more efficient and it makes building easier.
sentences.zh: 所以对蜜蜂来说，这更高效，也让筑巢变得更容易。

sentences.en: But humans benefit from that same efficiency and other structural features, which we'll get to later.
sentences.zh: 但人类也能从这种高效以及其他结构特点中受益，我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: So in this case, because this is a super efficient structural solution to lots of problems, bees and engineers, you know, kind of just came up with the same solution.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，由于这是解决许多问题的一种超高效结构方案，蜜蜂和工程师们，你知道的，就想出了相同的解决方案。

sentences.en: That makes total sense to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说完全说得通。

sentences.en: But in the midst of the modern era, another contingent came along and saw honeycombs as examples of intelligent design.
sentences.zh: 但在现代初期，另一派人出现了，他们将蜂巢视为智能设计的范例。

sentences.en: In the 1800s, one clergyman slash naturalist lauded bees as, quote, heaven instructed mathematicians, end quote.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，一位牧师兼自然学家赞美蜜蜂是“受天堂指引的数学家”。

sentences.en: Darwin actually saw this line of thinking as a big threat to his work, even in the 1850s, as he was writing On the Origin of Species.
sentences.zh: 达尔文实际上将这种思路视为对他工作的巨大威胁，甚至在19世纪50年代他撰写《物种起源》时也是如此。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: So why would the bees being good at geometry be a problem for evolution?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么蜜蜂擅长几何会对进化论构成威胁呢？

sentences.en: Great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: And so basically, if evolution is incremental, right, how do bees arrive at a perfect geometry?
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，如果进化是渐进的，对吧，蜜蜂是怎么得出完美的几何图形的呢？

sentences.en: Like, what are the steps they take?
sentences.zh: 比方说，它们采取了哪些步骤？

sentences.en: Because, you know, a slightly off, incomplete hexagon isn't a natural step towards making a good hexagon.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，一个稍微有点偏差、不完整的六边形，并不是通往完美六边形的自然步骤。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: It's just a bad shape.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个糟糕的形状。

sentences.en: And so where do we find the in-between versions?
sentences.zh: 那么我们在哪里能找到过渡版本呢？

sentences.en: And if there aren't any, the natural theological argument goes, somebody or some god must have handed the bees the answer.
sentences.zh: 如果没有的话，按照自然神学的观点，某人或某种神明一定把答案直接交给了蜜蜂。

sentences.en: Also, I suspect there was kind of a gut-level intuition behind all of this.
sentences.zh: 另外，我猜这一切背后其实有一种直觉。

sentences.en: Like, if you look around at the natural world, you see curves and fractals and all these chaotic things.
sentences.zh: 比如说，如果你环顾自然界，你会看到曲线、分形和所有这些混乱的东西。

sentences.en: But precise angular polygons are pretty weird and rare.
sentences.zh: 但精确的有角多边形非常奇怪且罕见。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so they seemed just visually like an exception to the norm, right?
sentences.zh: 所以从视觉上看，它们似乎是个例外，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So I can sort of see the argument or why it was complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以我多少能理解这个论点，或者明白为什么它会让人纠结。

sentences.en: And that was what had Darwin worried?
sentences.zh: 这就是让达尔文担忧的原因吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In fact, so much so that he actually kept bees to research and experiment on while he was writing origin.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正因如此，他在写《物种起源》时甚至还养了蜜蜂来做研究和实验。

sentences.en: And what he observed is that bees don't build hexagons outright.
sentences.zh: 他观察到的是，蜜蜂并不是直接建造六边形的。

sentences.en: They actually dig roundish holes that are, well, basically bee-shaped, right?
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是挖了一些圆形的洞，嗯，基本上就是蜜蜂形状的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But when a bunch of them do that, you know, in a grid, they end up bumping into each other.
sentences.zh: 但是当它们成群地在一个网格里这么做时，你知道的，它们最终会撞到彼此。

sentences.en: And as they approach their neighbors, they naturally make walls around those shared edges.
sentences.zh: 当它们靠近邻居时，它们自然会沿着那些共享的边缘砌墙。

sentences.en: And that turns into hexagons.
sentences.zh: 然后这就变成了六边形。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So they never really build a hexagon shape.
sentences.zh: 所以它们其实从来没有建造过六边形的形状。

sentences.en: Like, they dig a round hole and you put up some walls for support.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们挖了一个圆形的洞，然后你竖起一些墙来支撑。

sentences.en: And they're surrounded by other neighbors who are doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而它们的周围都是在做同样事情的邻居。

sentences.en: And the sides of the circular holes kind of push against each other and flatten out so that you get a hexagon shape.
sentences.zh: 圆形洞的边缘相互挤压并变平，最终你就得到了一个六边形的形状。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: None of which is to say that honeycombs aren't natural wonders.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说蜂窝不是大自然的奇迹。

sentences.en: In fact, Darwin was a huge fan.
sentences.zh: 事实上，达尔文是它们的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: And after he finished his research with these bees, he organized a whole section of origin around them and their honeycombs,
sentences.zh: 在他完成对这些蜜蜂的研究后，他在《物种起源》中专门用了一整节来讲述它们和它们的蜂窝，

sentences.en: in which he argued that these were amazing examples of the power of evolution.
sentences.zh: 他在其中论证了这些是进化力量的惊人例证。

sentences.en: And here's a little excerpt from that chapter.
sentences.zh: 以下是该章节的一小段摘录。

sentences.en: He must be a dull man who can examine the exquisite structure of a comb so beautifully adapted to its end without enthusiastic admiration.
sentences.zh: 谁要是能仔细审视这样一个结构精美、完美适应其用途的蜂房而没有满腔的赞叹，那他一定是个麻木的人。

sentences.en: We hear from mathematicians that bees have practically made their cells of the proper shape to hold the greatest possible amount of honey,
sentences.zh: 我们从数学家那里听说，蜜蜂实际上把它们的房室做成了能够容纳最多蜂蜜的形状，

sentences.en: with the least possible consumption of precious wax in their construction.
sentences.zh: 同时在建造时消耗最少宝贵的蜂蜡。

sentences.en: And, you know, there were already all of these connections.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当时已经有了所有这些联系。

sentences.en: But when Darwin published Origin, honeybees and hexagons became stuck together in one of the most popular science books of the century
sentences.zh: 但当达尔文出版《物种起源》时，蜜蜂和六边形在这个世纪最受欢迎的科学书之一中紧密结合在了一起，

sentences.en: and were essentially inextricably linked ever since.
sentences.zh: 并且自此基本上密不可分。

sentences.en: So when hexagonal panels are created around a century after Darwin, of course, they get named honeycomb panels.
sentences.zh: 因此，在达尔文之后大约一个世纪出现六边形面板时，它们理所当然地被称为蜂窝板。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, you're just naming them after what they look like, you know, like that makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你只是根据它们看起来像什么来命名，你知道的，这对我来说很合理。

sentences.en: But in terms of biomimicry, in terms of our subject today, were the aerospace engineers who were using the honeycomb shapes,
sentences.zh: 但就仿生学而言，就我们今天的主题而言，那些使用蜂窝形状的航空航天工程师，

sentences.en: were they building off of the logic of bees or were they building off the legacy of human researchers who came before them?
sentences.zh: 他们是建立在蜜蜂的逻辑之上，还是建立在前人人类研究者的遗产之上？

sentences.en: I mean, yes, I would say both, all of the above.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，我会说两者皆有，以上皆是。

sentences.en: And I rather dig that ambiguity, like there is no simple straight line from nature to humans.
sentences.zh: 我其实挺喜欢这种模糊性的，就像从自然到人类之间没有一条简单的直线。

sentences.en: And, you know, after 2,000 plus years of honeycomb history bringing us to the modern aerospace industry,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在经历了2000多年的蜂窝历史将我们带入现代航空航天工业之后，

sentences.en: you might think that that would be the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这已经是故事的结局了。

sentences.en: But I have one last little twist for you.
sentences.zh: 但我还有一个最后的反转要告诉你。

sentences.en: Oh, awesome.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: Okay, I want to hear more.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想听更多。

sentences.en: Yeah, so in the late 2010s, this 3D printing expert named Dhruv Bhatté got to thinking about honeycombs.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以在2010年代末，一位名叫德鲁·巴特的3D打印专家开始思考蜂窝的问题。

sentences.en: And he wondered if there was maybe more to them than this platonic ideal of this particular six-sided polygon.
sentences.zh: 他想知道，除了这种特定六边形多边形的柏拉图式理想之外，它们是否还有更多奥秘。

sentences.en: So he sought out an expert, an entomologist named Clint Pennick,
sentences.zh: 于是他找到了一位专家，一位名叫克林特·佩尼克的昆虫学家，

sentences.en: who was working at an actual biomimicry center at Arizona State.
sentences.zh: 当时他在亚利桑那州立大学的一个真正的仿生学中心工作。

sentences.en: And Clint was shocked to discover that Dhruv, who had built a whole career on honeycomb structures,
sentences.zh: 而克林特震惊地发现，德鲁虽然以蜂窝结构研究建立了自己的职业生涯，

sentences.en: had never even seen an actual honeycomb in real life.
sentences.zh: 却从未在现实生活中见过真正的蜂窝。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I worked in science for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我从事科学研究很长时间了。

sentences.en: This actually does not surprise me.
sentences.zh: 这其实并没有让我感到意外。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Because, you know, most engineers, they don't need to bother with bees.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，大多数工程师其实不需要去操心蜜蜂的事。

sentences.en: They know the shape, right?
sentences.zh: 他们知道形状，对吧？

sentences.en: But Clint sees this, and he starts showing Dhruv actual honeycombs.
sentences.zh: 但克林特看到了这一点，他开始向德鲁展示真正的蜂窝。

sentences.en: And together, they begin to look at how these vary by species.
sentences.zh: 他们一起开始研究这些蜂窝是如何因物种而异的。

sentences.en: And they observe that real honeycombs are actually quite a bit different from those sort of rigidly repetitive human-made honeycomb panels.
sentences.zh: 他们观察到，真正的蜂窝实际上与那些刻板重复的人造蜂窝板有很大不同。

sentences.en: Okay, so how did they differ?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那它们有什么不同呢？

sentences.en: Well, the easiest difference is at the corners, at these intersections that are sharply angled in human honeycomb panels,
sentences.zh: 嗯，最容易发现的区别在角落处，也就是人造蜂窝板上那些呈锐角的交汇处，

sentences.en: but in nature often have different degrees of rounding.
sentences.zh: 而在大自然中，这些地方往往有着不同程度的圆润过渡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I mean, that makes sense to me because, as Darwin described, you know, like the bees are kind of making a circle and it turns into a hexagon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对我来说说得通，因为正如达尔文所描述的，你知道，蜜蜂有点像是在画一个圆，然后它就变成了一个六边形。

sentences.en: So, like, not having other circles around you means that the edges are more rounded.
sentences.zh: 所以，周围没有其他圆圈意味着边缘会更加圆润。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: And so Clint and Dhruv use 3D printing to replicate those curves.
sentences.zh: 因此，克林特和德鲁使用3D打印技术来复制这些曲线。

sentences.en: And what they found is that they can offer real structural benefits.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，这些曲线能够带来真正的结构优势。

sentences.en: So ultimately, the pair got NASA funding to look even more closely.
sentences.zh: 最终，两人获得了美国宇航局的资金支持，得以进行更深入的研究。

sentences.en: And they x-rayed and characterized these different combs from dozens of different species of bees and wasps.
sentences.zh: 他们对来自几十种不同蜜蜂和黄蜂的各种蜂巢进行了X光透视和特征分析。

sentences.en: And they documented all kinds of smaller details, like the variations in the wall thicknesses and the way that separate comb sections are, like, joined together.
sentences.zh: 他们记录了各种更小的细节，比如壁厚的差异，以及不同蜂巢截面是如何连接在一起的。

sentences.en: And sure enough, subtler elements of the comb shape were found to improve structural performance with potential aerospace applications.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，蜂巢形状中更微妙的元素被发现能够改善结构性能，并具有潜在的航空航天应用前景。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, like, even in the Swayze age, bees are building better hexagons than we do.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至在这个时代，蜜蜂建造的六边形也比我们的更好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I mean, it depends upon the bee and the application.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这取决于蜜蜂的种类和应用场景。

sentences.en: But we are definitely still learning stuff from them, which is crazy.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实仍在向它们学习，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: I love that story.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: I mean, it makes me think about, you know, the very simple biomimicry story that we started with, this sort of Kingfisher bullet train story.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让我想起了我们一开始讲的那个非常简单的仿生学故事，那种翠鸟子弹头列车的故事。

sentences.en: You know, it's cool.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很酷。

sentences.en: It's easy to convey.
sentences.zh: 它很容易传达。

sentences.en: But it's pretty flat and flavorless by comparison.
sentences.zh: 但相比之下，它显得有些平淡无奇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I don't know if I'd go that far because there's something I really still dig about those straightforward biomimicry stories.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，我不知道我是否会走得那么远，因为我确实还是很喜欢那些直截了当的仿生学故事。

sentences.en: But sure, yes, there is something also richer, ultimately, about ones like the honeycomb story,
sentences.zh: 但当然，是的，像蜂窝故事这样的主题，最终也有其更丰富的一面，

sentences.en: where you have human creativity and nature ending up in this more complex back-and-forth conversation with one another.
sentences.zh: 在这里，人类的创造力和大自然最终形成了一种更复杂的、双向互动的对话。

sentences.en: Yeah, like a recursive discussion between nature and humans about, you know, the virtues of shapes, I guess.
sentences.zh: 对，就像大自然与人类之间关于形状价值的一场递归讨论，我想是的。

sentences.en: Kurt, this was so much fun.
